solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leads to man on board — on board!

indicators.note: on, in the sense of being aboard, says the chess man is placed inside the vessel

parts.note: boarding means going onto a ship, and SS, steamship, is the crossword ship
a pawn is a chessman, a piece on the board

explanation.surface: A chess pawn leads the way across the board, the setter delighted at the pun.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase changes sense: first the chessboard, then a ship, so the pawn goes between the two letters of the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To spawn is to generate or give rise to, so spawns works as a synonym of leads to.

clue.text: Student duo with soldier caught by rude man and fallen woman

indicators.note: being caught by someone means being held inside them, so the rude man contains the rest

parts.note: a carl (or churl) is an old word for a rough, ill-mannered fellow
L is a learner or student, so a pair of them is two Ls
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A pair of students and a soldier fall in with a boor and a disreputable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallen woman is the old-fashioned euphemism for a prostitute, which this hyphenated term also names.

clue.text: Brings in leftist regime, so struggle is set to worsen

parts.note: taken as written
to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: making the letters worse is read as breaking them up into a new order

explanation.surface: A commentator warns that a communist takeover will only make the conflict deteriorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to worsen' rearranges IS SET into TISES.
explanation.definitionFit: To sovietise a country is to impose a Soviet-style communist government on it.

clue.text: Send unsolicited mail and tinned meat

definitions.meaning: a verb for flooding inboxes with junk messages
the brand of canned luncheon meat famous in Britain since wartime rationing

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to send junk email and the noun is the famous brand of canned pork luncheon meat.

clue.text: I make mistake in capsize with strong wind off the point

indicators.note: a boat that capsizes turns over, so the mistake word is turned backwards

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
the levanter or levant is a strong easterly wind in the western Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A sailor confesses to a blunder when the boat overturned in a gale, though it hardly matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'strong wind' is the levanter or levant, the easterly that blows through the Strait of Gibraltar; 'in capsize' turns the error word over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irrelevant is beside the point, having no bearing on the matter in hand.

clue.text: King devoured 11's 28?

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ate means devoured

explanation.surface: A monarch gobbled up William's bad-tempered woman, the setter wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is WILLIAM and 28 is SHREW: Shakespeare's Taming of the Shrew features Katherina, called Kate; the theme's Prince William married Kate Middleton.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate is the headstrong heroine tamed in William Shakespeare's comedy, and also Prince William's bride in the theme.

clue.text: Treatment for 11's 28 cheers merciless emperor

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
Ming the Merciless is the tyrant emperor in the Flash Gordon stories

explanation.surface: A ruthless ruler is toasted with thanks for how he handles a difficult woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Shakespeare's play title The Taming of the Shrew, William being 11 and the shrew 28.
explanation.definitionFit: Taming is what Petruchio administers to Kate in Shakespeare's comedy, a cure for her temper.

clue.text: Intimate friend embracing Charles for instance?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the friend is placed around the other piece

parts.note: pal means friend
Charles is an example of ER's son, the Queen's son, read as ER plus SON

explanation.surface: A close companion hugs a man named Charles, perhaps a royal acquaintance.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina; Charles was the late Queen's son, giving ER + SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate and personal both describe something private, close to one's own life.

clue.text: Parking tricky as Europe in thick fog

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward or devious, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Parking becomes difficult in Europe when dense fog descends.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a dense yellowish London smog, so thick it resembled pea soup.

clue.text: An opening in stone

parts.note: the article gives A
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A gap in a stone wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious variety of chalcedony, a gemstone.

clue.text: Shakespeare's purpose early in the morning

parts.note: will means purpose or determination

indicators.note: the earliest part of the word in is its first letter

parts.note: AM is ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: The Bard rises with determination at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: William was Shakespeare's first name, so the possessive points to his given name.

clue.text: Those we fight see mine in detonation

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so these letters are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Soldiers watch a landmine explode.
explanation.definitionFit: Enemies are opponents or foes, the people one fights against.

clue.text: Runner outside failing to finish

indicators.note: not finishing means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: skin is the outside surface of a body

explanation.surface: An athlete drops out of the race before the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a runner, the long narrow blade that slides over snow, like a sledge runner.

clue.text: On time phone agent involved with military leadership

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A spy is rung punctually about a matter involving the top brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges PHONE AGENT into HEPENTAGON; 'On' places T first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon is the headquarters of the US Department of Defense, standing for the American military command.

clue.text: Battle pledge between 11 & 6

definitions.meaning: a military encounter or fight between forces
the promise to marry exchanged by William and Kate before their wedding

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a combat between armies and a formal agreement to marry.

clue.text: Artist acted with daughter in story that's nonsense

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the story

parts.note: a tale is a story
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
did means acted or performed

explanation.surface: A painter performs with his daughter in a tale that proves absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: A taradiddle is a petty lie or pretentious nonsense, an old-fashioned word for twaddle.

clue.text: 11's wide beer selection

parts.note: W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wide
ales are a range of beers

explanation.surface: William offers a broad range of beers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: William became Prince of Wales, so the principality is his by title.

clue.text: As 11 — until 19 27 — where radio frequency's knocked right out

indicators.note: with out, knocked out says one letter is ejected and replaced
completes the phrase knocked out, the right letter being thrown out for the frequency one

parts.note: wireless is the old British word for a radio set
F is the abbreviation for frequency

explanation.surface: William was single before the big ceremony, the old radio having lost its signal.
explanation.walkthrough: In WIRELESS the first R gives way to F.
explanation.definitionFit: Before his royal wedding William was without a spouse, unmarried.

clue.text: Journey very good to Indian state

parts.note: go means journey or travel
A is a top grade, very good

explanation.surface: A trip that works out well to a region of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is the small coastal state on India's west coast, a former Portuguese colony.

clue.text: Union for 11 & 6 where large dowry gained by deception

indicators.note: deceiving disguises the true order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A marriage where a big dowry was obtained through trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by deception' shuffles L, DOWRY and GAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: The wedding of Prince William and Kate in 2011 was a marriage of the royal family.

clue.text: Most tasty mum is yet to be seen out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Mother has not yet appeared to serve the most delicious dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Yummiest is the informal superlative of yummy, delicious.

clue.text: Fantastical horse gifted with ability to predict

indicators.note: fantastical means fanciful or bizarre, so these letters take an altered form

explanation.surface: A mythical talented horse can see the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Being foresighted means having foresight, the power to anticipate future events.

clue.text: Comment about second Gospel

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Mark is the second Gospel of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A remark about the second book of the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is an observation or comment.

clue.text: Crazy old woman died

parts.note: ma is mother, an old woman colloquially
D is the genealogical abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A deranged elderly lady has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad means crazy or insane.

clue.text: Sneer at 70s psychological treatment summary

parts.note: a dig is a sneering remark
EST, Erhard Seminars Training, was a 1970s self-improvement therapy

explanation.surface: Mocking a 1970s therapy fad in a brief review.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed summary of information.

clue.text: Puts up with unionist given thousand in cash payment

parts.note: to lump it is to put up with something unwelcome
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A trade unionist tolerates being offered a thousand as a single settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump sum is a single payment of money rather than instalments.

clue.text: Made as garment with four corners?

parts.note: the four corners of the earth are the compass points: south
east, the second compass point
west, the third compass point
north, the fourth compass point

explanation.surface: A tailor stitches a square cloth with four corners.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'four corners' of the world are the compass points S, E, W, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that is sewn has been made by stitching, the way garments are made.

clue.text: See 19
White Horse women have to go topless

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, so the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Women must dare to go bare-chested at a pub named the White Horse.
explanation.definitionFit: White horses are wave crests whipped into foam, so a white horse is a wave.

clue.text: Tiny animal's hour in work with needle

indicators.note: the hour letters go inside the sewing word

parts.note: to sew is to work with a needle

explanation.surface: A small creature spends an hour on needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew is a tiny insect-eating mammal like a mouse with a long snout.

clue.text: No waistcoat is worn by 50 international authors

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone surrounds them, so the waistcoat goes round the other letters

parts.note: a vest is a waistcoat, and with is read as the shortened 's it becomes vest's
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Fifty writers from around the world forgo waistcoats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is read as the contracted 's, so 'waistcoat is' gives VEST'S, i.e. VESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Novelists are writers of fiction, a kind of authors.
